samples.summary: The serve-mode `--fault` path — the one the explorer actually uses — has no test in any lane, and it is in fact broken
samples.evidence: The diff threads `fault` through `serve(browser, baseUrl, timeoutMs, fault)` (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:415) and through `openUiSession({ fault })` (hunt-ui-session.mjs), and `exploreUi` passes it (`openSession({ repoRoot: repo, fault })`, hunt-ui.mjs:307). But `serve()`'s call to `observeAction` at hunt-ui-runner.mjs:447-452 does NOT pass `fault`, so a seeded run through a live session silently navigates to the clean route. Nothing catches this: scripts/agent/hunt-ui-session.test.mjs never mentions `fault` (grep for `\bfault\b` across *.test.mjs returns only unrelated "session-fault" hits), and the new browser assertions in verify-hunt-oracles.mjs exercise only (a) direct `page.goto(...&fault=...)` and (b) `runUiPlan`, i.e. plan mode via `runAttempt`, which does pass `fault`. The new positive control is therefore untested on exactly the code path the hunter runs it on — the failure mode the diff's own comment calls 'worse than none'.

samples.summary: The new kebab-case `fault` validation added at three boundaries has no unit test at all, despite ready-made seams
samples.evidence: Three new validation branches ship in this diff: hunt-ui-runner.mjs parseArgs (`--fault must be a lowercase kebab-case id`), `runUiPlan` in hunt-ui-probe.mjs, and `openUiSession` in hunt-ui-session.mjs. None is exercised: grep for `\bfault\b` in scripts/agent/*.test.mjs finds no test, and hunt-ui.test.mjs never uses a fault value. Both files already have the exact seam such a test needs — `runUiPlan(..., { runner })` (hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs:233, with the sibling `attempts` validation test at :245) and `openUiSession({ spawnImpl })` with argv inspection (hunt-ui-session.test.mjs:57-60). So neither rejection of a malformed id (e.g. `x&surface=sheet`, `../x`, `A-B`) nor positive forwarding of `--fault <id>` into the child argv is covered; a regression that drops the flag or accepts arbitrary text passes green.

samples.summary: Test named "exploreUi returns the journal the tool actually wrote" asserts nothing about the journal — the writer is mocked away
samples.evidence: The test passes `createServerImpl: async () => ({})`, so the MCP tool that would append to `journal` never exists; `journal` is necessarily the empty array created inside `exploreUi`. The only journal assertion is `assert.ok(Array.isArray(out.journal))`, which holds regardless of whether any journal wiring works. The load-bearing assertions are the prompt markers (RUBRIC-MARKER / TASK-MARKER / 'at most 5 browser actions'), which are fine — but the title claims coverage of journal plumbing the mock removes.
searchedFor: read hunt-ui.mjs exploreUi (journal created locally, handed to createServerImpl)

samples.summary: runHunt's new `fault` parameter is never asserted to reach exploreImpl or runPlanImpl
samples.evidence: `runHunt` now takes `fault` and forwards it to `exploreImpl(...{ fault })` (hunt-ui.mjs:938), `runPlanImpl({...}, { fault })` (:1023) and `replayUiCandidate(..., { fault })` (:1024). The funnel tests stub all three impls and could trivially capture the option, but no test passes `fault` to `runHunt` or asserts it appears in the stub's received options — so a dropped forward (the same bug class that exists in serve mode) escapes the cheap stubbed funnel tests this file exists to provide.
searchedFor: read hunt-ui.test.mjs funnelDeps and every runHunt test

samples.summary: installFault's documented modifier-key exemption (Ctrl/Meta/Alt keys must NOT be swallowed) is untested
samples.evidence: `installFault` deliberately exempts modified keys so undo etc. is unaffected — the comment says the control must inject 'ONE defect, not a fog'. `checkSeededFault` asserts only the declared attribute, unknown-id ignoring, and drop/no-drop of plain typing; nothing types a modified key under `?fault=drop-second-char` and asserts it still takes effect. A regression there would make seeded runs validate a different, wrong defect shape while still passing.
searchedFor: glob packages/frontend/src/app/harness/** for unit tests (none exist)

samples.summary: cmdPreflight — the documented mandatory gate before any spend — has no test
samples.evidence: .claude/commands/hunt-ui.md step 1 makes `hunt-ui.mjs preflight` the gate that 'nothing else works until it passes', and it contains real logic (runner existence, playwright presence in packages/frontend, per-persona validation, lazy SDK import, token presence, exit 1 on problems). hunt-ui.test.mjs imports loadPersonas/validatePersona/selectPersonas/runHunt but no preflight entry point, and cmdPreflight is not exported, so nothing exercises it. A preflight that always passes is indistinguishable from a working one in CI.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. hunt-ui-runner.mjs threads `fault` into serve() (:415, called with args.fault at :523) but serve()'s observeAction call at :447-452 omits it, while plan mode's call at :472 includes it; runAction only appends `&fault=` from that parameter (:244). The explorer reaches the runner through this serve path (hunt-ui-session.mjs:115-118 spawns `--serve` + `--fault`; hunt-ui.mjs:307 openSession({repoRoot, fault})). Searching the whole tree (excluding .trusted/) for the literal `--fault`, for `drop-second-char`, for `openUiSession`, and a word-boundary `fault` grep restricted to any *test* file, I found no test that exercises serve-mode fault seeding: the only fault coverage is verify-hunt-oracles.mjs's direct page.goto checks (:296,:305,:311) and checkPredictionFunnel driving runUiPlan (:392-398), which is plan mode via hunt-ui-probe.mjs:309. hunt-ui-session.test.mjs's argv test (:54-70) asserts only `--serve`/absence of `--plan`. CI wiring (package.json:16 -> scripts/verify-browser-lanes.mjs:72) adds no session lane. A new behavior (seeded positive control for explorer sessions) shipped with no meaningful test on the path it runs on — missing-test, major under the test-adequacy rubric. No counterexample found.

verdict.reason: The three kebab-case `fault` guards exist (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:79-81, hunt-ui-probe.mjs:286-288, hunt-ui-session.mjs:107-109) and none is exercised by any test. I enumerated every `test(` in hunt-ui-probe.test.mjs (28-329) and hunt-ui-session.test.mjs (50-240): no fault case, even though the exact seams are present (injected `runner` at probe:228-242 next to the tested `attempts` guard at 244-246; argv-inspecting `spawnImpl` at session:54-70). hunt-ui.test.mjs has no `fault` token; hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs's `fault` hits are the unrelated "session-fault" refusal (395-409, 560); packages/frontend/scripts has no test file, so runner `parseArgs` is untested. Repo-wide greps for `--fault`/`kebab` outside node_modules surface only source, docs, and .agent-review artifacts. The one real counterexample candidate, verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:291-332 and 392-398, drives fault forwarding end-to-end through runUiPlan and does weaken the reviewer's "positive forwarding is uncovered" sub-claim — but it is a Chromium-dependent `pnpm verify:hunt:oracles` script that only ever passes a valid id and never reaches a rejection branch. No counterexample exists for the finding's actual subject: rejection of a malformed fault id is untested at all three boundaries, so accepting arbitrary text would pass green.
